## Novelty pre-check

Verdict: **trivial_or_ill_posed**. The statement ends at “with” before specifying k in PurathSecond. The choice matters because the earlier assessment reports that p = 521 defeats the reading “for some k ≥ 2” while leaving the reading k = v₂(p−1) viable. The Lean declaration names Forberg and PurathThird without defining them. The full conjunction therefore cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text. The absence of a resolving R-ref does not establish openness.

- **Classify each prime by a complete recurrence cycle and test the choice of $k$** [succeeded, finite computation]: Completed exact parity-aware cycles for 239 of 239 primes through 1500. ([code](computations/mrl_bea0e081.py), [result](computations/mrl_bea0e081.result.json))
  - [Computational Mathematician] The run covered all $239$ primes $p\le1500$. Returning to the initial Fibonacci pair, Lucas pair, and index parity certifies every subsequent index for each tested prime. The absent primes below $150$ agree exactly with the quoted list. For every odd prime in range, Lucas absence, an odd Fibonacci zero, and odd Fibonacci rank agreed. For every $5<p\le1500$, the maximal-$k$ test agreed with Lucas absence. The existential-$k$ test first disagreed at $29$. These are exhaustive comparisons over the stated primes.
- **Measure Lucas entry indices and all hit residues modulo prime powers** [succeeded, finite computation]: Completed 55 of 55 prime-power cycles. Each completed residue list describes every index for its modulus by periodicity. ([code](computations/mrl_4c3722d4.py), [result](computations/mrl_4c3722d4.result.json))
  - [Computational Mathematician] All $55$ cycles completed, and the predicted least positive entry and full set of zero residues agreed in every case. The effective range was exactly the prime powers $p^m\le1849$ with $p\le97$ and $m\ge1$. This range can be recovered despite the truncated table. The displayed rows exhaust $44$ powers through base $43$, including $43^2=1849$. The rows for $2$ stop at $2^{10}$, so the modulus bound was below $2048$. Each of the remaining $11$ cases must therefore be a first power, giving the consecutive primes from $47$ through $97$. Each completed period certifies all indices for its modulus. The finite comparison alone does not settle lifting for arbitrary primes or exponents.
